test_title: PYST 49: SSC CPO - General Knowledge and General Awareness (Held on 03 Oct, 2023 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: In India, which of the following regulatory mechanisms was NOT in existence to enforce regulation of the industrial sector?

options.text: Industrial licensing under which every entrepreneur had to get permission from government officials to start a firm, close a firm or decide the amount of goods that could be produced.
Controls on price fixation and distribution of selected industrial products.
Private sector was allowed in all industries.
Some goods could be produced only in small-scale industries.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Private sector was allowed in all industries.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Industrial licensing:-**

 
 
• **It was a system in place in India that required entrepreneurs to obtain permission from the government to start, close, or expand their businesses. **
 
• This system was in place from the 1950s to the 1990s, and it was designed to control the growth of the industrial sector and ensure that it was in line with the government's economic planning.
 
• Controls on price fixation and distribution of selected industrial products were also in place during this time period.
 
• These controls were designed to protect consumers from exploitation by ensuring that prices were fair and that goods were distributed evenly.
 
• **There were a number of industries that were reserved for the public sector, meaning that only the government could own and operate businesses in these areas. **
 
• These industries included coal, steel, railways, and aviation.
